planting.note: Plant container divisions in spring in well-drained, lean to moderately fertile soil in full sun; Junior Walker stays noticeably smaller and tidier than Walker's Low, fitting a border edge or container where the larger cultivar would sprawl.

directions: Junior Walker is a compact selection bred from Walker's Low, holding the same aromatic, silver-gray foliage and abundant lavender-blue flower spikes but on a smaller, tighter mound that better suits a border edge, small bed, or container than its larger parent. It blooms heavily from late spring into summer, and shearing the plant back by about half after the first flush encourages a strong rebloom into fall. Plant in well-drained, lean to moderately fertile soil in full sun, since rich or wet soil causes floppy, open growth. It is highly drought-tolerant and deer-resistant once established, needing little more than the occasional post-bloom shearing to stay dense and tidy.

common_name: Tuscan Sun Heliopsis (Compact Golden False Sunflower)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container plants in spring in well-drained, average to fertile soil in full sun; Tuscan Sun stays noticeably shorter and more compact than the species, reducing the need for staking.

directions: Plant in well-drained, average to fertile soil in full sun; Tuscan Sun is a compact selection of false sunflower bred to stay under 2 feet tall, well below the 3-5 foot height of the straight species, while still producing the same abundance of bright golden-yellow, daisy-like flowers from early summer through fall. Its sturdy, self-supporting stems rarely need staking despite the heavy bloom load, and deadheading spent flowers extends the bloom season further. It tolerates heat, humidity, and average garden soil with ease, and is a strong nectar source for bees and butterflies as well as a good cut flower. Divide congested clumps every three to four years in spring to maintain vigor and flowering.

common_name: Desert Eve Red Yarrow (Compact Non-Flopping Red Yarrow)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container plants in spring in very well-drained, lean soil in full sun; Desert Eve Red was bred from seed for a compact, sturdy, non-flopping habit that holds up better in heat and humidity than older yarrow seed strains.

directions: Plant in very well-drained, lean soil in full sun; Desert Eve Red bears flat-topped clusters of deep cherry-red flowers with a lighter center over finely cut, aromatic, gray-green foliage, on a compact plant bred specifically to resist the flopping and splaying that afflicts many older yarrow varieties in humid climates. It blooms from late spring through summer, and deadheading spent flower heads encourages continued bloom. Like all yarrow it is extremely drought- and heat-tolerant, performing best in lean, dry soil rather than rich or consistently moist ground, which encourages crown rot in humid Gulf South summers. Divide every two to three years in spring to keep the clump vigorous and prevent it from thinning out in the center.

common_name: Desert Eve Yellow Yarrow (Compact Non-Flopping Yellow Yarrow)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container plants in spring in very well-drained, lean soil in full sun; part of the same compact, non-flopping Desert Eve seed strain as Desert Eve Red, bred for sturdier habit in heat and humidity.

directions: Plant in very well-drained, lean soil in full sun; Desert Eve Yellow bears flat-topped clusters of bright golden-yellow flowers over finely cut, aromatic, gray-green foliage on a compact, sturdy plant bred to resist the flopping habit of older yarrow seed strains. It flowers from late spring through summer, and cutting back spent blooms encourages continued flowering and a tidier appearance. As with all yarrow, drought tolerance is excellent and rich or consistently moist soil should be avoided, since it invites crown rot in hot, humid conditions. Divide the clump every two to three years in spring to renew vigor and keep the center from thinning.
